instruction: Use command line tools to sort the Age column in the opened ods file in ascending order and export the result as 'sorted_by_age.csv' on the Desktop.

metadata.explanation: Task requires sorting ODS file by Age column in ascending order. Verified with Python: when sorted by age ascending, the first 5 rows all have age=21 (there are multiple people aged 21). Agent should convert ODS to CSV, then sort by Age column (column 6) using command line tools (e.g., sort -t',' -k6 -n). Evaluator checks if the first 5 data rows in the output CSV have Age values of [21, 21, 21, 21, 21].

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts ALL values from Age column (not just first 5), providing complete dataset access

Metric performs comprehensive verification: checks first 5 values are minimum (21), verifies consecutive ordering at beginning (50 rows), middle (50 rows), and end (50 rows), validates min/max values are reasonable
Multi-point sampling strategy effectively catches sorting errors across entire dataset (~5000 rows)
Edge case handling: checks for empty data, type conversion errors, insufficient rows

Minor logic inefficiency: The every-10th-value check (lines 52-54) only validates consecutive pairs instead of sampled intervals, but this doesn't affect correctness due to comprehensive consecutive checks at key regions
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional improvement: Change line 52-54 logic from 'int_values[i] > int_values[i + 1]' to 'int_values[i] > int_values[min(i + 10, len(int_values) - 1)]' to properly check monotonic ordering across sampled points
